body: Toll Services: Your vehicle has an unpaid toll balance of $6.99. To avoid a $50 late fee, pay by today: https://tollpay-renew.top/us
explanation: Toll agencies don't text payment links from foreign numbers. The odd ".top" link and the scary late fee are the giveaways.

body: Delivery Co: Your package is on hold due to an incomplete address. Update within 12 hours or it will be returned: http://redeliver-parcel.info/a7
explanation: Delivery companies don't text from random email addresses. An unexpected "fix your address" link is a classic way to steal card details.

body: YOUR BANK: A charge of $1,249.00 at ElectroMart was flagged. If this wasn't you, call our fraud department now at (888) 555-0199.
explanation: Scammers fake fraud alerts and put their own number in the text. Call the number on the back of your card instead.

body: Hi Mom, it's me. My phone fell in the sink so this is my new number. Can you text me back here? I need a quick favor.
explanation: "New number, need a favor" is a family-impersonation trick. Call your child on their old number before doing anything.

body: "Grandma? It's me... I'm in trouble. I was in a car accident and I'm at the police station. Please don't tell Mom. My lawyer will call you about bail. He says it has to be gift cards or cash today."
explanation: Panic, secrecy and gift cards are the grandparent scam. Voices can be cloned with AI, so hang up and call your grandchild directly.

subject: Your subscription renewed: $399.99
body:
Thank you for renewing SecureShield Total Protection for 3 years. Amount charged: $399.99.

Didn't authorize this? Call our refund desk within 24 hours: 1-888-555-0143.
explanation: Fake renewal invoices push you to call a "refund desk" that then asks for remote access or bank details. Check your real statements instead.

body: Hi! I'm a recruiter for a digital marketing agency. Earn $300–$800 a day rating products from home, just 30 minutes a day. Interested? Message me on Telegram @hr_lucy_joblink 😊
explanation: Unsolicited job offers with huge pay for simple tasks are "task scams." Moving you to another chat app is another red flag.

body: Hi, is this David? It's Ava from the yoga studio, are we still on for dinner Friday? 😊
explanation: A friendly "wrong number" text is often the first step of a long investment or romance scam. Don't reply; just delete it.
situation: You don't know anyone named Ava, and your name isn't David.

body: I'll take it! I can't meet so I'll send a courier. Please scan this QR code to verify your account so you can receive my payment.
explanation: Real buyers never need you to scan a code or "verify" an account to pay you. The QR code leads to a fake payment page.

body: So sorry, I accidentally sent you $850 instead of $350! Can you refund the extra $500 with gift cards or Zelle? I'll send the courier for the bike after.
explanation: This is the overpayment trick. The first payment is fake or gets reversed, and you're out the "refund" you sent.

body: Congrats! You've been selected to receive a $1,000 gift card from a major retailer. Claim before midnight: bit-claim-reward.co/gift
explanation: You can't win a prize you never entered. The link collects your personal and card information.

subject: You are eligible for a tax refund of $1,384.17
body: After the last annual calculation, you are eligible to receive a refund. Submit your bank details within 48 hours to receive your payment.
explanation: Tax agencies don't email you asking for bank details. A ".com" address with "gov" stuffed in the name is fake.

body: "This is Officer Brown from the federal benefits office. Your benefits number has been suspended due to suspicious activity. Press 1 now to speak with an agent or a warrant will be issued."
explanation: Government agencies don't suspend your number or threaten arrest by robocall. Hang up and don't press anything.

body: STATE DMV NOTICE: Your driver's license will be suspended on 10/30 due to unpaid traffic violations. Pay now to avoid suspension: dmv-state-pay.xyz
explanation: DMVs don't suspend licenses by text with a payment link. The ".xyz" web address is a clear fake.

subject: Your account is on hold
body: We couldn't process your last payment. Update your payment details within 24 hours to keep watching.
explanation: Look closely: "supp0rt" uses a zero. Look-alike addresses plus a payment link mean phishing. Open the app yourself instead.

body: Hi, sorry to bother you! I accidentally sent my verification code to your number. Could you text it back to me? It's really urgent 🙏
explanation: That code was sent to YOU because someone is trying to take over your account. Never share a code with anyone.

body: My love, I'm stuck on the oil rig and my bank card is blocked. I just need $2,000 for the customs fee so I can finally come home to you. I'll pay you back the day I land ❤️
explanation: An online love interest you've never met in person who needs money for an "emergency" is a romance scam.

subject: Payment sent: $799.99 to CryptoHub
body:
You sent $799.99 USD to CryptoHub LLC.

If you did not make this payment, call PayFlow Support at +1 (877) 555-0156 immediately.
explanation: Fake receipts make you panic and call the scammer's number. Check your payment app directly instead.

body: Cloud Storage: Your storage is full. Your photos and videos will be deleted on 10/31. Upgrade now with 90% off: cloudsave-offer.shop
explanation: Your phone's real storage warnings appear in Settings, not in texts with ".shop" links and deadlines.

body: 5 viruses detected. Your personal data and bank accounts are at risk. Do not close this window. Call Certified Tech Support now: 1-888-555-0177
explanation: Web pages can't scan your device. Pop-ups with a phone number are tech-support scams. Just close the tab.

body: City Power & Light: Your power will be disconnected in 30 minutes due to an overdue bill. Call 1-800-555-0102 now to pay with a prepaid card.
explanation: Utilities send written notices and never demand prepaid cards. The 30-minute deadline is there to rush you.

subject: Congratulations! You're hired
body: You have been selected for a remote Data Entry position ($45/hr). We will mail you a check to purchase equipment from our approved vendor. Please deposit it and send the vendor payment today.
explanation: Being hired without an interview, then asked to deposit a check and pay a "vendor," is a fake-check scam. The check will bounce.

body: I made $12,000 last month with this AI trading bot 🚀 My mentor only takes 5 new students. DM me "PROFIT" to join the VIP group!
explanation: Promises of guaranteed profits and a secret "VIP group" are investment scam bait.

body: FINAL NOTICE: You qualify for full student loan forgiveness under the new program. Approval closes TODAY. Call 855-555-0190 to lock it in.
explanation: Real loan programs never cost money to apply and don't close "today." Check only through your official loan servicer.

body: Yes, it's still available! I'm working overseas, so I can't show it. Wire the $1,200 deposit and I'll mail you the keys.
explanation: A "landlord" who can't show the place and wants a wire is a rental scam. Never pay before you see the home in person.

body: Your international parcel is held at customs. A $2.99 release fee is required. Pay here: parcel-customs-release.com
explanation: The small fee is a trick to get your card number. Customs doesn't text you from a foreign number.

body: "This is your bank's fraud department. Your account has been compromised. To protect your money, we need you to move it to a new safe account today. If the teller asks why, tell them it's for a home repair."
explanation: Banks never ask you to move money to a "safe account" or lie to a teller. Caller ID can be faked. Hang up and call your bank.

body: OMG is this you in this video?? 😮 tinyurl-video.cc/xr8
explanation: Hacked friend accounts send shocking "is this you?" links to steal your login. Check with your friend another way.

subject: Password expires today
body: Your email password will expire in 2 hours. To keep using your current password, confirm it below.
explanation: No real service asks you to "confirm" your password through an email link. This page steals it.

body: Help hurricane victims NOW! Every dollar counts. Buy gift cards and text the card numbers to this number. God bless.
explanation: Real charities never collect gift card codes by text. Give through a charity's official website.

body: "This is Deputy Lewis with the county sheriff's office. You missed jury duty and there's a warrant for your arrest. You can settle the fine today with prepaid cards to avoid being taken in."
explanation: Courts don't call to collect fines with prepaid cards or threaten arrest by phone. Hang up and call the court's official number.

subject: 0.5 BTC ready to withdraw
body: Your trading account has earned 0.5 BTC. To release your withdrawal, a 10% unlock fee must be paid first.
explanation: Having to pay a fee to get your own "profits" out is the final stage of a crypto investment scam.

body: You're pre-approved for a $15,000 personal loan, no credit check! Pay a $150 processing fee to release your funds: quickloan-fast.biz
explanation: Legit lenders don't charge upfront fees to release a loan, and they do check credit.

body: Congrats!! 🎉 You won our tablet giveaway! Just pay $4.95 shipping here within 1 hour to claim your prize: sunny-claim.shop
explanation: Copycat "giveaway" accounts ask for a small shipping fee to grab your card. Real giveaways don't charge winners.

subject: Mark Thompson shared "Invoice_Oct.pdf" with you
body: You have received a secure document. Sign in with your email address and password to view it.
explanation: An unexpected file that needs your email password to open is a login-stealing trap.

body: Before I come see the couch I want to make sure you're real. I'm texting you a 6-digit code, just read it back to me.
explanation: They're using your number to set up an account in your name. Never read a code to anyone.

body: BANK ALERT: Unusual sign-in detected. Your online access has been locked. Verify your identity now: secure-bank-verify.co/login
explanation: Banks don't send login links like this. Open your bank's app or type its address yourself.

situation: You're logging into your bank's app and just tapped "Send code."
body: Your Bank: Your verification code is 482913. We will never call you to ask for this code. Don't share it.
explanation: You asked for this code, it has no link, and it warns you not to share it. Just type it into the app yourself.

situation: You have a dentist appointment next Tuesday.
body: Bright Smile Dental: Reminder of your appointment Tue 11/4 at 2:30 PM. Reply C to confirm or call our office to reschedule.
explanation: It matches an appointment you made and asks for nothing but a confirmation. That's a normal reminder.

situation: You dropped off a prescription yesterday.
body: Your prescription is ready for pickup at Main St Pharmacy. Reply STOP to opt out.
explanation: It's expected, has no link and asks for no payment or personal details.

situation: You ordered a lamp online two days ago.
subject: Your order #20491 has shipped
body: Good news! Your order is on its way. You can track it anytime by signing in to your account on our website or app.
explanation: It matches your real order and doesn't pressure you. Still, tracking through the store's own app is the safest habit.

situation: Your daughter flew to Denver today.
body: Hey Mom, landed safe! Grabbing my bag now, I'll call you tonight ❤️
explanation: It's from her saved number, fits what's happening, and asks for nothing.

situation: You have a checkup with Dr. Patel tomorrow.
body: "Hi, this is Karen from Dr. Patel's office calling to confirm your appointment tomorrow at 10. If you need to reschedule, please call the office. Thanks!"
explanation: A simple confirmation with no request for money or information is normal.

situation: You just tapped "Forgot password" on a shopping site.
subject: Reset your password
body: We received a request to reset your password. If this was you, use the button below. If not, you can ignore this email.
explanation: You started the reset just now, and the sender matches the store. Reset emails you didn't request are the ones to ignore.

situation: You just bought groceries at Corner Grocery.
body: Your Bank: Did you attempt a $62.18 purchase at Corner Grocery on 10/28? Reply YES or NO. We'll never ask for your PIN or passcode by text.
explanation: It matches your real purchase, has no link or phone number to call, and only asks YES or NO.

situation: You're expecting a furniture delivery today.
body: Your Northwind Home order will be delivered today between 2 and 4 PM.
explanation: Expected, no link, no fee, no request. Just information.

body: Are we still on for coffee Saturday at 10? ☕ I'll save us a table by the window.
explanation: A friend making plans, asking for nothing. Not every message is a trap!

subject: New this month at your library
body: Free tech help sessions every Wednesday at 2 PM. No sign-up needed. Bring your phone or tablet and your questions!
explanation: Pure information with no link to click, no login and no payment.

situation: Your grandchild goes to Lincoln Elementary and a big storm is coming.
body: Lincoln Elementary: School is closed tomorrow due to weather. Stay safe!
explanation: It fits the situation and asks for nothing. That's a normal school alert.

body: Hi! Is the bike still available? I could come see it Saturday morning and pay cash.
explanation: Seeing the item in person and paying cash is how safe local deals work. Meet in a public place.

situation: You dropped off a prescription this morning.
body: "This is an automated message from Main St Pharmacy. Your prescription is ready for pickup. No action is needed."
explanation: Expected and asks you to do nothing. No pressure, no payment.

situation: You just bought a coffee maker online.
subject: Thanks for your order!
body: Order total: $49.99. Estimated delivery: Friday. You can view your order anytime in your account.
explanation: It matches what you just bought and doesn't ask you to call, pay or log in through a link.

situation: You've been streaming a lot of videos this month.
body: Your Wireless: You've used 75% of your monthly data. No action needed. Usage resets on the 1st.
explanation: An informational alert with nothing to click and nothing to pay.

situation: You just booked a ride in a ride-share app.
body: Your driver Carlos is arriving in 2 min in a silver sedan, plate 7KDL203.
explanation: It matches the ride you just booked and asks for nothing.

situation: Your company announced open enrollment last week.
subject: Reminder: open enrollment ends Friday
body: Open enrollment ends this Friday. To make changes, log in to the HR portal the way you usually do. Questions? Visit HR on the 3rd floor.
explanation: It points you to the portal you already use instead of a link, and matches what your company announced.

situation: You put your name on a restaurant's waitlist.
body: Your table at Rosa's Kitchen is ready! Please check in with the host within 10 minutes.
explanation: You asked to be texted and it asks for nothing but showing up.

body: Happy Paws Vet: Max is due for his annual checkup. Call us at the number on your pet's records to book.
explanation: A routine reminder that sends you to a number you already have. No link, no payment.

subject: Your October statement is ready
body: Your monthly statement is ready. For your security, we never include links in our emails. Sign in to our app to view it.
explanation: No link, no pressure, and it tells you to use the app you already have. That's what real banks do.

body: "Hi Grandpa, it's Sam! Just calling to say hi. Call me back on my cell when you can. Love you!"
explanation: It's from Sam's saved number, there's no emergency and no money request.

situation: You put a book on hold last week.
body: Your hold "The Lighthouse Mystery" is ready. Please pick it up by 11/5.
explanation: It matches something you did and needs nothing from you.

situation: You signed up for a yoga class tonight.
body: Reminder: Your yoga class starts at 6 PM tonight. See you there!
explanation: An expected reminder with nothing to tap or pay.
